output.name: Sekul

output.myth: In the year of the great thaw, Tavo the Gale laughed and the valleys ran full. Brown water came down off the hills and sank the lower boats at their moorings, and the children stood in the shallows with nothing but their hands. Aun was on the cliff mending a kite, and he was ashamed that his knife had let so much loose sky. He took the gourd from his own boat, scraped it clean and bored a handle through its neck. Then he went down into the flood and bailed for three days without sleep. When he was done his palms were raw and every boat was floating. Hesk the Reel counted them and found none lost. She wound the gourd up on a string and hung it in Vel, where the thaw could see it. Now when the floods come down, Sekul rises over the Lamp Road, and the people go to the water with their own gourds.
output.verse:
Thaw down the valleys,
boats fill; Sekul climbs the sky,
hands raw, still bailing.

Only the alternative 'teapot or kettle with a curved spout' comes close.

Stars 50583 (top knob) and 50564 (lower edge of the knob) sit almost on top of each other, so the knob reads as one dot.
The bowl is a loose blob with no clear rim or depth, and its outline runs into the spout area.

Gold skeleton lines are correct and a blue silhouette exists, so it is a real outline. The figure is upright: handle up, bowl down, drops falling below the lip.
Drop stars 47205 and 47310 sit on the thin drop outlines and are correct. Lip 46774 and base 49029 are roughly on the right parts.
